# sonarqube_project_branch_retention (Resource)

Keeps one branch of a project when it becomes inactive ("Keep when inactive" in the UI): housekeeping, which deletes branches not analyzed for `sonar.dbcleaner.daysBeforeDeletingInactiveBranchesAndPRs` days, skips it. Destroying the resource lets housekeeping delete the branch again. The branch must exist, i.e. have been analyzed; branches other than the main one need Developer edition or above. The main branch is always kept. To keep the branches created from now on whose name matches a pattern, add the pattern to the list setting `sonar.dbcleaner.branchesToKeepWhenInactive` (default `main`, `master`, `develop`, `trunk`); patterns do not apply to existing branches. Import ID: `project/branch`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Keep the release branch when it is no longer analyzed. The branch must
# already exist: it is created by its first analysis.
resource "sonarqube_project_branch_retention" "release" {
  project = "my-project"
  branch  = "release/1.x"
}

# To keep branches created from now on whose name matches a pattern, extend
# the list setting; it replaces the default list, so repeat the defaults.
# Patterns do not apply to branches that already exist.
resource "sonarqube_setting" "keep_release_branches" {
  key    = "sonar.dbcleaner.branchesToKeepWhenInactive"
  values = ["main", "master", "develop", "trunk", "release/.*"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `branch` (String) Branch name, e.g. `release/1.x`.
- `project` (String) Project key.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `project/branch`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import sonarqube_project_branch_retention.example 'my-project/release/1.x'
```
